title: Refactor EKS control plane Terraform module for cross-account KMS and rolling upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The existing EKS control plane Terraform module works for single-account provisioning but lacks patterns we need for cross-account KMS usage, clearer separation of control-plane vs nodegroup permissions, and a safe automated upgrade path for private clusters. Scope: Move module to a more opinionated layout that supports: 1) optional cross-account KMS key attachment for secrets/etcd encryption; 2) dedicated IAM roles for control-plane operations and for bootstrap/eksctl interactions; 3) upgrade hooks that trigger prober checks and can abort/rollback; 4) a lightweight health-check stack (CloudWatch metrics + Prometheus exporter sidecar pattern) configurable per environment. Goals: 1) Make upgrades predictable and idempotent in customer VPCs; 2) Reduce blast radius when rotating KMS keys or changing IAM; 3) Provide observability surfaces required for SRE runbooks and incident playbooks; 4) Keep terraform composition compatible with existing provisioning pipelines so existing customers are not forced to migrate immediately. Constraints and decisions: - Use AWS provider exclusively for control-plane resources (no eksctl binary required in module). - KMS: support two modes: in-account KMS key (default) or customer-provided cross-account key ARN with a minimal key policy the module can attach via IAM role assumption. We will not attempt to automatically re-encrypt existing secrets in-place; that will be a follow-up migration job. - Upgrades: EKS control plane version upgrades in AWS are strongly coupled to nodegroup compatibility. This module will expose a controlled upgrade workflow: terraform plan/apply updates nodegroup launch template / ASG first, run health probes, then trigger EKS version bump. - Health checks: export cluster endpoint and nodegroup health metrics to CloudWatch with an opt-in prometheus exporter helm chart; module will render a HelmRelease resource compatible with Flux/Argo in customers that use GitOps. Deliverables: - Refactored terraform module with clear inputs/outputs and examples for single-account and cross-account KMS. - Integration test harness that runs in our CI sandbox account to provision a throwaway cluster and validate upgrade path and health probes. - Documentation PR for Console and on-prem runbooks and a security signoff.
acceptance_criteria: Module accepts a customer KMS key ARN and applies the minimal IAM permissions required to let EKS use it for secrets encryption (or falls back to managed key when absent)
Control-plane IAM roles are separated from nodegroup/bootstrapping roles and documented in the module outputs
Terraform plan/apply for a non-destructive minor upgrade (e.g., 1.24 -> 1.25) succeeds in CI sandbox and health-checks pass post-upgrade
Module exposes a boolean flag to enable the health-check stack and verifies that CloudWatch metrics for node readiness and kube-apiserver latency are emitted
Security team has approved KMS cross-account pattern and IAM role assumption model (security signoff attached)
tasks: Design module interface and update README with examples for cross-account KMS
Implement IAM role separation and new input variables (kms_key_arn, control_plane_role_arn, bootstrap_role_arn)
Add upgrade workflow helpers: plan-checker, prober lambda, and abort-on-failure hook
Add opt-in health-check resources: CloudWatch alarms, Prometheus exporter helm chart values
Create CI integration test that provisions cluster, deploys sample app, performs rolling node upgrade and then control-plane version bump
Open PR and request security and SRE review; iterate on feedback
comments: 2026-03-02 Aisha Patel: Kickoff sync with SRE and Security. Agreed KMS cross-account must use explicit role assumption and a minimal key policy. Security asked for an audit-only mode first before enabling automatic re-encryption.

2026-03-04 Markus Chen: POC terraform snippet added to branch feature/ENG-11847-kms-poc. POC demonstrates attaching policy to customer key via assume-role; raises question about who rotates key alias — added to tasks.

2026-03-06 SRE (Jordan Lee): Health-check requirements posted. Suggested metrics: node_ready_count, kube_apiserver_request_duration_seconds (p90). Prefer CloudWatch exporter over pushing custom lambdas for customers who want minimal footprint.

2026-03-08 Security (Priya Rao): Requested explicit list of allowed principals for cross-account key access and a plan to log key usage to CloudTrail with at least 30-day retention. Also requested threat model doc — created link in attachments.

2026-03-10 Markus Chen: Initial implementation complete. Opening draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-private/pull/462. CI sandbox tests failing on 'kubectl port-forward' step due to EKS endpoint access from CI locked by SG. Retrying with bastion egress approach.

2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Reviewed PR and left comments around variable naming and outputs. Noted that docs need a migration note: customers with existing encryption-config must run re-encrypt job and module should not attempt this automatically. Security review scheduled for 2026-03-14.
notes: Consider adding a migration-helper actuator in a later sprint that talks to the kube-apiserver with customer consent.
If CI sandbox continues to block EKS endpoint access, next step is to build a small ephemeral bastion that works via SSM SessionManager instead of opening SG egress in customer-like accounts.
